newsitem.title: FRANCE: French shares trade lower, rumours weigh.
newsitem.headline: French shares trade lower, rumours weigh.

text.p: French shares traded lower on Thursday morning with investors taking profits ahead of the end of the trading month on Friday and due to rumours related to the election, traders said.

"There is talk in the market of a secret poll which gives the right a small majority," said a head trader at a German bank in Paris. "But the problem with secret polls is that nobody has really seen them," he added.
At 0827 GMT, the CAC-40 was down 0.85 percent at 2762.64. The May future was 20 points lower at 2,760.
There is a ban on the publication of opinion polls during this last week to the May 25 date for the first round in the parliamentary election.
But financial firms and political parties are nevertheless ordering private polls from the polling institutes.
"I think this is a normal decline at the eve of the liquidation (end of the trading month) and with an election in the weekend," a trader said.
He warned that the first-round voting leave an unclear picture with fragmented voting and a high abstention rate.
At 0843 GMT, the CAC-40 had extended its losses to 2755.45, down 1.11 percent.

Elf-Aquitaine, the heaviest weighting in the CAC-40 index, was up 2.34 percent at 612 francs after a statement that Renault was selling a 0.9 percent stake in the company to Elf unit Financiere Valorgest.

Traders said the share was up because the market expected Elf to cancel the shares at a later stage and also because some investors had gone short in Elf on the back of rumours of a pending placement of shares.
Renault was down 2.72 percent at 150.30 francs. A company spokesman said the Elf shares had been bought in 1994 at 411 francs per share.
Peugeot was also down, falling 2.32 percent to 632 francs.
CLF-Dexia France was a rare riser with a 1.13 percent increase to 539 francs. It has a shareholders' meeting today.
